explain.title: How catch rate works
explain.intro: Every species has a catch rate from 3 to 255: 3 for the hardest, such as Mewtwo, 255 for the easiest, such as Caterpie. Each throw turns that number, the HP left, the status condition and the ball into one figure, the modified catch rate a. From Generation 5 on:
explain.legend: MaxHP and HP are the wild Pokémon's maximum and current HP, Rate its species' catch rate, Ball the ball's multiplier and Status the status bonus.
explain.hp: At full HP the HP part works out to a third; at 1 HP it is almost one. Knocking a Pokémon down to 1 HP with False Swipe nearly triples your odds, and red HP is nearly as good.
explain.status: Sleep and freeze multiply a by 2.5 (by 2 before Generation 5); paralysis, poison and burn by 1.5. Sleep is the best status to inflict, and the Dream Ball works best on a sleeping Pokémon.
explain.shake: If a is 255 or more, the Pokémon is caught. Otherwise the game works out a shake value b and makes shake checks: each passes if a random number from 0 to 65535 is below b. The ball wobbles once for each check that passes, and the Pokémon is caught only if every check passes. From Generation 6 there are four checks:
explain.shakeGens: Generation 5 made three checks with b = 65536 ÷ (255 ÷ a)^(1/4). Generations 3 and 4 made four with b = 1048560 ÷ √(√(16711680 ÷ a)), which works out to a chance of about a ÷ 255.
explain.level: Sword & Shield make a wild Pokémon under level 20 easier to catch, multiplying a by (30 − level) ÷ 10. Scarlet & Violet do the same under level 13, by (36 − 2 × level) ÷ 10.
explain.balls: A Great Ball multiplies a by 1.5 and an Ultra Ball by 2. Special balls do far more in the right situation, and each one's multiplier changed over the generations: the calculator uses the right value for the game you pick, and shows why each ball is strong or weak right now.
explain.left: Critical captures (a rare throw that needs only one shake check), Generation 5 bonuses such as dark grass, and the penalty in Sword & Shield and Scarlet & Violet for a Pokémon above the level your badges allow, so real odds can be a little higher or lower. The games round each step, which this calculator doesn't, so it can differ by a fraction of a percent. Max HP assumes average IVs. Legends: Arceus and Let's Go use different catch systems and aren't covered.
